records.summary: A configurable tracker for private landlords and letting agents to record hazard reports, repair deadlines and supporting evidence. It is intended to help them manage requirements if Awaab’s Law is extended to private rentals; the exact rules and start date remain unsettled.
records.how_money: Landlords or letting agents pay; no price is specified.
records.market: England; the sources discuss extending Awaab’s Law to private rented tenancies.

competitors.name: Harthing
competitors.note: Launched a competing rental repair/compliance product on 12 May 2026, according to its founder.

competitors.name: Letavo
competitors.price: Free for up to 3 properties; £9/month for unlimited
competitors.note: Advertises rental repair and compliance features; its builder case study labels the launch May 2026.

competitors.name: Lettie
competitors.price: Free for up to 4 properties; then £2.50 per property/month
competitors.note: Advertises maintenance reporting and repair features; a press release dated 4 August 2026 announced its free maintenance-reporting plan.

competitors.name: Landlord Studio
competitors.note: Offers compliance tracking and reminders.

competitors.name: LandlordGuard
competitors.note: Offers compliance tracking and reminders.

competitors.name: Lettable
competitors.note: Advertises landlord software.

competitors.name: Fixflo
competitors.price: £75/month software fee plus quoted pricing; contractor marketplace from £0.30/unit/month
competitors.note: Listed pricing applies to customers with at least 50 properties; offers repair and audit features.

competitors.name: LetSync
competitors.note: Advertises a repair-tracking service scheduled to open on 15 December 2026; not yet launched as of 23 October.

rounds.plain: The idea was seen but not validated. The exact regulation timing and paid demand remain uncertain.

The consultation says 2027 is the earliest feasible start, so the need had not been withdrawn or delayed beyond 2028. No private-rental deadline workflow was found in the listed incumbent products at that check.

risks: Regulations must still set the requirements; the roadmap lists the date as TBC.
No dated, verifiable revenue or paid-customer evidence was found.
Direct competitors already advertise free entry tiers and overlapping repair or compliance features.
Owner hours and the share of work that can be automated are unverified; urgent escalations and rule updates may require manual work.
A possible proprietary repair-outcomes dataset is only a future idea; it does not yet exist.
records.moat: Weak at launch. Rules are unsettled and competitors already advertise similar audit reports and repair histories. A trusted case history and CRM integrations could create switching friction, but a proprietary anonymised repair-outcomes dataset is only a possible future asset.
records.next_steps: Run the one-day no-code test: check exact-intent search volume in Google Ads Keyword Planner without filling in missing values, make a branded report-to-clock-to-evidence mockup with a clearly priced pilot offer, and share it once in a landlord forum that permits research posts. Measure opt-ins and paid intent; do not cold-message individual landlords.

records.summary: A portfolio planner for private landlords that maps EPC metrics, upgrade evidence and exemptions. The proposed product would help landlords plan and document work against the new MEES standard, whose compliance date is 1 October 2030.
records.how_money: Landlords pay; no specific price for the proposed product is given.
records.customer: Private landlords, particularly those managing multiple properties.
records.market: England; the sources also discuss EPC data coverage in England and Wales and a separate service in Scotland.

revenue_claims.claim: Government estimates the policy could result in 1.75 million homes receiving upgrades by 2030; this is an upgrade estimate, not a count of likely software buyers.
The 2024 English Private Landlord Survey reported about 513,000 direct landlords in its deposit-scheme sample; 17% had five or more properties, representing 49% of tenancies.
The 2024 English Housing Survey found 48% of private rented dwellings at EPC C and 37% at D; these are legacy EER figures, not homes failing the new dual-metric standard.

records.paid_demand: No independently verifiable revenue, paid-customer count or completed sales evidence for a direct private-landlord MEES planner was found. Competitor prices and free tiers are advertised offers, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: LandlordEPCs
competitors.price: Free planner; £14.99 full plan; additional properties £9.99 each
competitors.note: Direct planner advertises multi-property comparison, simulated improvements, exemption checks and a PDF roadmap.

competitors.name: PropReady
competitors.note: Markets an EPC upgrade planner and portfolio upgrade planning.

competitors.name: Lettable
competitors.note: Its £49 plan includes MEES strategy and EPC planning.

competitors.name: Duewise
competitors.price: £9.99 monthly or £99 yearly for its standard plan

competitors.name: Stead
competitors.note: Closed beta began May 2026, according to its press page; includes EPC lookup, not a confirmed costed MEES planner.

competitors.name: Cotality
competitors.note: Describes an established portfolio retrofit product used by landlords of over two million homes; small-landlord fit and pricing are unclear.

rounds.plain: The idea was seen but not validated. A future planning need may arise, but paid demand was unverified and a free direct planner and other portfolio tools exist.

The 2030 MEES requirement was confirmed, and the check found one adjacent landlord/EPC launch, not two qualifying launches or five qualifying incumbents. Later research found a direct free planner, so the generic planner's differentiation is weak.

risks: The legislation was planned to come into force in 2027, subject to Parliamentary approval; detailed rules and metrics may change.
A direct competitor advertises a free planner, and other vendors market EPC planning.
EPC records and policy rules are public, which lowers imitation barriers.
No competitor revenue, willingness to pay, acquisition costs, automation share or owner hours are verified.
The 2024 landlord survey predates the 2026 policy decision and does not fully represent landlords whose agents register deposits.
records.moat: No strong moat is established. EPC records and policy rules are public, and direct competitors already advertise free or low-cost planners. A permissioned history connecting property evidence, invoices and assessor-confirmed upgrade outcomes could become an asset, but it does not yet exist.
records.next_steps: Make a privacy-safe sample portfolio report using public EPC data and published policy rules, then compare it directly with the free LandlordEPCs planner. Keep only a specific portfolio-evidence or workflow gap. Offer a clearly labelled, refundable £14.99 reservation through a permitted landlord community or opt-in audience, and count only actual reservations as demand evidence.

records.summary: A self-serve sandbox for finance software teams to validate invoices and test migrations ahead of UK VAT e-invoicing. It would use versioned rules, migration comparisons and developer integrations; the detailed UK specifications are still pending.
records.how_money: The proposed customer is software teams, but the sources do not specify the product’s pricing model.
records.customer: Finance software teams preparing for UK VAT e-invoicing.
records.market: United Kingdom; the planned mandatory VAT e-invoicing start is April 2029, with detailed specifications and legislation planned by the end of 2027 to 2028.

revenue_claims.claim: Quadient reported French e-invoicing bookings grew eleven-fold year over year in Q2 2026 and included a multi-million-euro white-label agreement with a software provider. Bookings are commitments, not recognized or collected revenue, and this was a broader platform rather than a UK migration sandbox.

records.paid_demand: No direct revenue for a UK-specific sandbox or evidence that software teams will pay for one was found. Adjacent sandbox and validator prices are advertised offers, not sales evidence.

competitors.name: peppol.sh
competitors.price: Unlimited free sandbox; €0.20 per live invoice, falling to €0.10–€0.16 at higher top-ups
competitors.note: Generic Peppol developer sandbox and live delivery; launch listing dated 18 October 2026.

competitors.name: eFaktúra
competitors.note: Developer portal launched 31 May 2026; sandbox began 30 May and moved to the real OpenPeppol test network on 10 June, according to its changelog.

competitors.name: European Commission validator
competitors.note: Provides a validator, REST/SOAP APIs and a conformance test bed.

competitors.name: Invoicetronic
competitors.note: Pricing includes validation.

competitors.name: Ironfang
competitors.price: 250 free monthly validations, then £2 per 1,000 in its first paid usage tier
competitors.note: Adjacent validation offer.

competitors.name: Transalis eInvoice/Peppol
competitors.note: G-Cloud listing includes a sandbox.

rounds.plain: The idea was seen but not validated. UK rules and software-team willingness to pay remain unverified.
HMRC confirmed mandatory VAT e-invoicing from April 2029, with standards and technical specifications planned by the end of 2027 to 2028. The check found no rule that killed the idea before then.

risks: The immediate buyer market is a narrow, uncounted set of software teams; population figures mainly describe invoice users or VAT traders.
Adjacent products and the European Commission offer free sandboxes or validators, making a paid sandbox alone difficult to justify.
HMRC may supply or endorse a conformance suite, and existing providers may bundle testing.
UK rule details are pending; a dependable product depends on those specifications.
The 28 October 2026 roadmap was still upcoming as of the assessment date.
records.moat: Low at first. Basic validation is easy to copy because Peppol standards and free validators are public. A versioned UK rules engine, synthetic test corpus, migration diffs and CI integrations could create switching costs once embedded, but those assets do not yet exist.

hours.note: Unverified estimate after the product and ruleset update process are stable; roadmap changes and enterprise support could push this higher.

records.next_steps: After the 28 October roadmap, prepare a branded landing page and synthetic invoice/API-result demo, clearly label UK rules as pending and accept no real invoices. Publish in opt-in software-developer channels and ask for a paid pilot commitment; continue only if a finance software team commits to pay.

records.summary: Software to validate packaging producer data files and flag reporting errors before submission. Packaging producers would pay, but DEFRA's free file generator already includes validation and can check files created elsewhere.
records.how_money: Packaging producers pay; no price for the proposed product is specified.
records.customer: Packaging producers that submit EPR data.
records.market: United Kingdom; the sources describe packaging EPR reporting deadlines.

competitors.name: DEFRA/PackUK packaging data file generator
competitors.note: The 2026 generator has built-in validation, can check files producers created themselves, and produces pre-validated CSVs.

rounds.plain: K3 means a platform owner or partner already serves the need. DEFRA's free generator directly covers file validation and produces pre-validated CSVs.

risks: Buyer appetite and whether existing free tools adequately serve the need are unverified.

records.summary: An evidence ledger connecting packaging producer data to records from accredited reprocessors or exporters for closed-loop reporting. It would help producers link waste data to eligibility evidence and prepare reporting records.
records.how_money: Producers pay; no specific price for the proposed product is given.
records.customer: Packaging producers reporting eligible closed-loop packaging waste.
records.market: United Kingdom; the reporting requirement applies to 2027 data onwards.

revenue_claims.claim: There were 344 UK packaging direct registrants in the 2025 compliance year; this is not the total producer population or the eligible closed-loop market.
The statutory closed-loop registration fee is £2,548 per year; this is paid to the regulator, not a software vendor.

records.paid_demand: No dated paid-revenue event for a directly comparable closed-loop evidence ledger was verified. A competitor publishes prices, but that does not show completed sales.

competitors.name: pEPR Packaging Reporter
competitors.price: £25, £50 and £90 monthly plans, or £250, £500 and £900 yearly
competitors.note: Broad pEPR reporting product; closed-loop evidence features are unverified.

competitors.name: PackTotal
competitors.price: Quoted initial implementation cost and annual licence
competitors.note: Prices are not published.

competitors.name: Valpak Global Data Insights
competitors.note: Platform launch reported on 16 April 2026; covers packaging, supplier data, EPR costs and reporting.

competitors.name: Lappa
competitors.note: Its 22 September 2026 newsletter says its Shopify-to-EPR integration is in pilot.

competitors.name: Normantics
competitors.note: Advertises UK EPR evidence-linked records and document extraction, but says it is in development.

rounds.plain: The idea was seen but not validated. The eligible segment is narrow, key registration deadlines have passed, and a continuing paid workflow is unproven.
The check found no evidence that the free reporting service links closed-loop evidence to producer data. PackUK handles filing and validation, but evidence-ledger functionality was unverified.

risks: The 1 October 2026 deadline to register for 2027 closed-loop data has passed.
The eligible segment is much narrower than the general packaging EPR population, and its size is unverified.
PackUK's central service handles registration, submissions, automated validation and fee calculations; compliance schemes can also register members.
The proposed concept alone has no moat; public registers and the reporting service provide much of the underlying data and process.
Owner hours, software revenue and demand are unverified; disputed evidence and onboarding could require recurring manual work.
records.moat: No moat is established in the concept alone. A permissioned history linking producers, packaging lots, operator evidence, accreditation status and validation could become an asset, but it does not yet establish producer-side switching costs.
records.next_steps: Download the current producer and accredited-reprocessor registers, identify producers with public evidence of eligible food-grade plastic collection or tray-to-tray recycling, and mock up evidence upload, eligibility checks and report export. Seek a paid pilot or evidence pack through opt-in channels or compliant outreach to verified corporate subscribers.
